title: Deployment Options
learning_outcomes: Explain hosted model apis and how it connects to deployment options.
Apply managed model platforms in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for deployment options and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers deployment options through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Design for production: deployment boundaries, throughput, latency, cost, monitoring, recovery, prompt/model versions, CI/CD, and ongoing maintenance.
content.why_it_matters: Hosted model APIs belongs to the application integration boundary. Validate inputs before sending them, keep credentials on the server, handle non-success responses and cancellation, and log request metadata without storing secrets or unnecessary personal content. Provider-specific payloads must be checked against the selected API's current documentation.

items.text: Use managed model platforms as a lens for understanding deployment options. Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

items.text: Use self-hosted inference to reason about behavior under real workloads, not just a successful local example. Measure latency and cost on representative requests, define operational limits and rollback options, and test what happens when dependencies slow down or fail.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet to a local file such as lesson_example.py and run it with Python 3.11+ using `python lesson_example.py`. This is a local/static teaching example; CodeLeaf's current browser iframe previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript and is not a secure Python runner. Do not paste API credentials into the example or public source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and fixed sample inputs, rerun it, then change one input at a time and compare the new output with the stated contract.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice hosted model apis within deployment options: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: Deployment Options is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
Use explicit inputs, criteria, and reproducible examples to test the concept.
Document uncertainty, failure modes, security considerations, and version assumptions.
